purpose: One vocabulary for Vaultix. Use the term; when the owner says one of owner_says, name the term once and continue. Do not add a new word for something listed here. status says what exists, read from the repo on the seeded date. The owner corrects this file; an AI proposes changes and never rewrites an owner-corrected entry.

terms.meaning: The Vaultix product everyone gets: secrets, UI, API. Never gated.
The only place code for the hosted paid service lives. It may depend on the engine; the engine never depends on it.
terms.status: folder and check built; no code yet

terms.meaning: One self-contained folder per feature holding its API, service, store, UI, tools and tests.
terms.status: decided; applied per domain during the Go port

terms.meaning: One product to the customer, separate modules underneath, each owning its own data.
terms.vaultix_name: Nomen + Vaultix + Wardenclyffe joined by contracts

terms.meaning: The service that creates, upgrades, backs up and bills customer instances. It holds no secret values.
terms.status: planned after the main instance and classifier endpoint exist

terms.meaning: Each hosted customer gets their own running copy of the engine and its database.
The AI sees a name or handle for a secret, never the value. Also called an opaque handle or indirection.
owner_says: the AI only gets the name

terms.meaning: A trusted service puts the value into the target process at the moment of use. Also called just-in-time (JIT) injection.
owner_says: hands the key to the app
terms.status: CLI run built; redeem flows partly built

terms.meaning: The value travels on a path the AI is not on.
The line a value may not cross.
Each identity can do only what its job needs. A scoped token is the usual tool.
owner_says: can only write to that org

terms.meaning: An identity for a machine, app or AI agent, as opposed to a person. Also called workload identity.
The AI shows a link; the person signs in and approves; the AI gets a time-limited session.
terms.vaultix_name: the user's session for AI clients
terms.status: Go service issues codes (off by default); approval page, CLI support, MCP admission and renewal missing

terms.meaning: Blocking outbound paths so data cannot be sent out.
Detecting sensitive data and removing or masking it before it leaves. Removal is redaction.
terms.status: scanning and canary built; classifier planned

terms.meaning: The owner's own model, run in the cloud service, that labels and organizes sensitive values. Each endpoint serves one org, is one-way, and writes only to that org's space. Designed for many accounts; more copies start at peak hours.
terms.status: planned; not built. Whether copies are bound to one org or shared is undecided

terms.meaning: One model plans and never sees sensitive data; another handles the data and cannot act outside. Also called privileged and quarantined models, or planner and executor.
owner_says: the reasoning AI gives directions and the machine bot writes
frontier works with the local one

terms.meaning: An agent with private data, untrusted input and a way to send data out is exploitable. Remove one and the attack fails.
Content the AI reads tricks it into misusing its own access. The misuse is the confused-deputy problem; the leak is exfiltration.
A person must approve before an action runs. The check is an approval gate.
terms.status: general service built for certificates, code signing and PAM; one flow for every action is draft ADR 0125, not saved

terms.meaning: The rule for an action: who the approvers are, how many approvals are required, and the enforcement level (hard or soft).
Ordered approval steps, each with its own approvers. Later steps are the fallback.
The submitter may approve their own request. On a one-person account this is the only option and is an accepted single point of failure.
Where a request stands.
The phone's face or fingerprint check signs an approval and the server verifies the signature. The standard is WebAuthn.
terms.status: WebAuthn code exists; not wired to approvals

terms.meaning: The site added to the phone's home screen, able to receive push notifications.
terms.status: not built: no manifest, service worker or push

terms.meaning: One action framework so a person, the API and an AI all run the same handler, permission check and audit.
One MCP endpoint per domain, listing only that domain's tools.
terms.status: 8 of 15 live in the repo; none on the live instance as of 2026-11-12

terms.meaning: One of the 15 product areas that name folders, routes, warp points and UI actions.
terms.vaultix_name: public, auth, workspace, secrets, access, automation, connect, pki, kms, pam, detect, ai, governance, operate, experience

terms.meaning: A named, scripted step in the real UI that an AI or a walkthrough can trigger while the person watches.
owner_says: impersonate the operator in front of them
terms.status: 16 named, 5 working locally; no backend command

terms.meaning: The server's record that an action really happened.
One agreed vocabulary used by the people, the code and the docs.
Mapping whatever words someone uses to the one canonical term. Also called entity linking.
owner_says: a signal so the AI sees it bright

terms.meaning: Giving the AI the smallest set of facts that makes it right the first time.
